unit.title: Databases and SQL for school records

lesson.title: Joining tables for reports
lesson.subtitle: JOIN and LEFT JOIN, who's missing, and reports with only what's needed

video.title: Joining tables for reports
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Mr Joseph — computer studies teacher, Kenya (main character)
Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, peer to peer)

scenes.visual: Icon cards: Pupils + marks; Two vanished; A whole term. Mr Joseph beside it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: I joined our pupils table to the marks, and sent the report to the head. Two pupils had vanished from it. Nobody noticed for a whole term.

scenes.visual: Paper-grey title card: the Darsi mark, the course name and the lesson title with the Data engineering track chip.
scenes.animation: Mark scales in with a small overshoot; the title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: joining tables, and reports that show only what's needed.

scenes.visual: Code typed out on a card: SELECT p.name, m.mark … Caption: ON: how the rows match, by key
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: A join puts rows side by side
scenes.narration: A join puts rows from two tables side by side. JOIN names the second table, and ON says how rows match: the mark's pupil number equals the pupil's id.

scenes.visual: Two columns: “JOIN” (Only matches; No mark? Gone) and “LEFT JOIN” (Every pupil; No mark? NULL).
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: Inner keeps matches; left keeps all
scenes.narration: A plain JOIN is an inner join: it keeps only rows that match. A pupil with no mark simply vanishes, without a word. LEFT JOIN keeps every row of the first table, and fills the gaps with NULL.

scenes.visual: Code typed out on a card: SELECT p.name … Caption: Kept by the left join, with no mark
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: So, to find the pupils with no mark, use a left join and keep the rows where the mark is NULL. That's the list of who missed the test.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: Two marks: two rows; Inner join: rows can vanish; Count before and after.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Joins can multiply rows too. A pupil who sat the test and a resit appears twice, once per mark. So count before and after: are rows missing, or counted twice?

scenes.visual: Quiz card: the question with its answer options.
scenes.animation: Answer cards drop in one by one.
scenes.narration: Quick check! I do an inner join of pupils and marks. What happens to a pupil who has no mark?

scenes.visual: Icon cards: Left out, silently; My two pupils; Use LEFT JOIN.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: They're left out, silently. That's how my two pupils vanished. When every pupil must appear, use a left join.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: A parent: their child only; The head: class averages; Never: phones, health notes. Dr Farah beside it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Now think about who reads the report. A parent needs their own child's marks. The head needs averages per class. Nobody needs phone numbers and health notes in a marks report.

scenes.visual: Icon cards: Only needed columns; Only their rows; The rest stays in.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: So select only the columns each reader needs, and only their rows. A join can bring in everything; a good report query leaves most of it out.

scenes.visual: Icon cards joined by arrows: Inner, then left; Who disappears?; Who appears twice?.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: In the app, try each join of pupils and marks. Watch who disappears, who appears twice, and how the count of rows and the count of marks drift apart.

scenes.visual: Quiz card: the question with its answer options.
scenes.animation: Answer cards drop in one by one.
scenes.narration: Your turn. A report for parents' evening goes to each family. Which columns should it show?

scenes.visual: Summary card: JOIN on a key; Inner drops, left keeps; Missing, or twice?; Only what the reader needs. Takeaway bar: Join to answer; then leave out what isn't needed.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Just the child's name and their own marks, for that family only. Remember: a join matches rows on a key. Inner joins drop what doesn't match; left joins keep it as NULL. And a report shows only what its reader needs.

scenes.visual: Rows of icon and text: Parent, nurse, head; Sort the column cards; Which does nobody need?. Dr Farah beside it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Try it in class tomorrow: ask your pupils what a parent, the school nurse and the head teacher each need from the school records. They sort column cards into three piles. Which columns does nobody need at all?

checkpoints.prompt: An inner join of pupils and marks: what happens to a pupil with no mark?

options.text: They're left out of the result
The query stops with an error

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — an inner join keeps only matching pairs, so a pupil with no mark is silently left out.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — there's no error and no zero: an inner join simply leaves the pupil out. A left join keeps them, with NULL.

checkpoints.prompt: A report for parents' evening goes to each family. What should it show?

options.text: Name, class, every mark, phone and health notes
Their child's name and their child's marks

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — each family needs its own child's name and marks, and nothing about other children.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — phones and health notes don't belong in a marks report, and other children's marks aren't a parent's business.
